To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
pain education can be defined in three dimensions, namely target, impact and strategies.
pain education is a multidimensional and multifaceted concept that requires a three-dimensional perspective.

• The target dimension of pain education is the learner, the content, and the environment • The impact dimension is the outcome, the process and the evaluation • The strategy dimension is the curriculum, the delivery method, and the assessment.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a three-dimensional approach to pain education, which will provide an overview of pain education and help to develop a comprehensive and integrated pain education curriculum.
the development of an evidence-based, multidimensional framework to guide the development of pain education programs.
how to improve the education of healthcare professionals in pain medicine, and how to improve the quality of pain education for patients.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

pain education is the systematic process of acquiring and applying knowledge, skills and attitudes to promote the understanding and management of pain, which can be delivered through different strategies and impact on the target audience at different levels.
pain education is an important and challenging field, and the three-dimensional approach can provide a useful framework to understand and define the educational aspects of pain medicine.
pain education is a three-dimensional approach, and it should not be considered in isolation, but rather in the context of the whole educational environment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
pain education is a multidimensional process, with a variety of target groups and educational strategies that have a broad impact on the healthcare system.
the target of pain education is the individual patient, the impact is the improvement of pain care and the strategy is the use of a multidisciplinary approach.
pain education is a multidisciplinary process that aims to enhance the understanding of the multidimensional nature of pain in order to improve patient care.
The main takeaway from our work is that
pain education is not only a matter of providing knowledge to healthcare providers but also a matter of changing the attitudes and behaviors of healthcare providers.
the pain education strategy should be tailored to the needs of the target audience, and that the impact of education should be measured to improve its effectiveness and efficiency.
a multidimensional approach to pain education will be required to address the complex needs of pain education.
